recipes.name: Field Perch and Mustard Greens Soup
recipes.description: A northern-style clear soup made with small field perch, mustard greens and ginger. The fish is simmered first and the strained cooking liquid becomes the broth, while the picked meat is returned to the pot.
recipes.serving_basis: Four bowls of soup to share with a family rice meal.
recipes.finished_dish: Flaky perch and tender mustard greens sit in a light, ginger-scented broth.
recipes.serving: Serve hot as part of a rice meal.
tips: Strain the fish broth carefully and check the meat for pin bones.
Add greens near the end so they stay bright and tender.
recipes.image_alt: Clear field perch soup with green mustard leaves and fine ginger; transparent background.
ingredients: Scale, clean and remove gills and entrails.
Wash and cut into serving pieces.
Use half to boil the fish and half sliced.
For boiling fish and making soup.
For cleaning the fish and seasoning.
preparation_steps: Scale and clean the fish; rub lightly with salt, rinse and drain.
Wash and cut mustard greens. Bruise half the ginger, slice the rest and mince the shallot.
Prepare a fine strainer and a clean bowl; check carefully for bones when picking the fish.
cooking_steps: Boil water with bruised ginger and a pinch of salt. Add fish and cook until just done; remove and cool slightly.
Pick the fish meat and check for small bones. Strain the broth; sauté shallot and briefly toss the fish with a little pepper.
Bring the strained broth to a boil, add sliced ginger and mustard greens and cook for 1–2 minutes.
Return fish to the pot, season with fish sauce and salt, simmer gently and serve hot.

recipes.name: Pomelo, Shrimp and Pork Salad
recipes.description: A light Vietnamese pomelo salad combines separated pomelo segments with boiled shrimp, sliced pork belly, carrot, Vietnamese coriander and a sweet-sour fish-sauce dressing. The dressing lightly coats the ingredients so the pomelo stays intact.
recipes.serving_basis: Four appetizer portions or a shared side dish.
recipes.finished_dish: Juicy shrimp and tender pork balance crisp pomelo, carrot and herbs under a bright sweet-sour dressing.
recipes.serving: Plate and top with crushed roasted peanuts; serve immediately after mixing.
tips: Cool the cooked shrimp and pork completely before mixing.
Add dressing gradually and toss gently to keep pomelo segments whole.
recipes.image_alt: Pomelo salad with shrimp, thin pork slices, carrot, Vietnamese coriander and roasted peanuts; transparent background.
ingredients: Separate segments; remove seeds and thick membranes.
Reduce if the pomelo is tart.
preparation_steps: Rinse shrimp and pork. Separate pomelo into segments, remove seeds and thick membranes; shred carrot and chop herbs.
Mix fish sauce, lime juice, sugar and minced garlic until the sugar dissolves; adjust to a balanced sweet-sour taste.
Bring water to a boil for cooking the shrimp and pork separately; cool both completely before mixing.
cooking_steps: Boil pork belly until cooked, briefly cool in water, then slice thinly.
Boil shrimp just until cooked; cool, peel and split lengthwise if large.
Combine pomelo, shrimp, pork, carrot and herbs. Add dressing a little at a time and toss gently.
Taste, plate and sprinkle with roasted peanuts. Serve immediately.

recipes.name: Hanoi Herbal Chicken Noodle Soup
recipes.description: Hanoi mì gà tần combines chicken braised with traditional herbal seasoning and mugwort, served with egg noodles. This Bếp Việt version adapts the street dish to a home pot with cut chicken pieces.
recipes.serving_basis: Four bowls of egg noodles with herbal chicken, mugwort and broth.
recipes.finished_dish: Tender chicken remains in pieces in a fragrant herbal broth; mugwort has a gentle bitterness and egg noodles stay springy.
recipes.serving: Blanch noodles separately, add chicken and mugwort, ladle over hot broth and finish with scallion and pepper.
tips: Simmer the herb pack first so the broth is fragrant but not bitter.
Cook chicken until just tender; avoid over-braising.
Blanch noodles separately to keep the broth clear and noodles firm.
recipes.image_alt: Bowl of Hanoi herbal chicken noodle soup with braised chicken, golden egg noodles, mugwort and dark broth; transparent background.
recipes.time_note: About 1 hour 50 minutes, including 15 minutes to marinate the chicken.
ingredients: Use a packaged food seasoning blend.
preparation_steps: Rinse chicken and pat dry. Rub lightly with salt, rinse again, then marinate with a little fish sauce and pepper for 15 minutes.
Rinse the herbal pack, dates and goji berries. Bruise the ginger and shallots; pick and wash the mugwort.
Bring a separate pot of water to a boil for the noodles.
cooking_steps: Add the herbal pack, ginger, shallots, dates, goji berries and water to a pot. Bring to a boil, lower the heat and simmer for about 20 minutes.
Add the chicken, bring to a gentle boil and skim. Simmer 35–45 minutes until just tender; season with fish sauce, salt and pepper.
Add mugwort for the final 5–8 minutes and cook until just tender.
Blanch noodles as directed, divide among bowls, add chicken and mugwort, ladle over broth and garnish with scallion and pepper.

recipes.name: Mekong Delta Lá Mơ Cake with Coconut Sauce
recipes.description: A soft, chewy Mekong Delta steamed cake gets its natural green color from lá mơ leaves and combines rice flour with tapioca starch. It is served with lightly thickened coconut sauce and toasted sesame.
recipes.serving_basis: About 12 small steamed cake pieces with coconut sauce.
recipes.finished_dish: Green, chewy cake pieces are topped with rich coconut sauce and fragrant toasted sesame.
recipes.serving: Cut into pieces, pour over warm coconut sauce and sprinkle with sesame.
tips: Strain the leaf juice finely for a smooth batter.
Stir continuously while heating the batter to prevent lumps.
recipes.image_alt: Green lá mơ steamed cake topped with coconut sauce and toasted sesame; transparent background.
search_terms: green herb steamed cake coconut sauce
ingredients: Blend with water and strain for green juice.
Divide between batter and coconut sauce.
Wash and blanch to line the steamer.
preparation_steps: Wash lá mơ, blend with water and strain through a fine sieve to obtain green juice.
Whisk rice flour, tapioca starch, leaf juice, 150 ml coconut milk, some sugar and salt until smooth; rest for 5 minutes.
Wash and soften banana leaves for lining the steamer. Toast sesame until fragrant.
cooking_steps: Cook the batter over low heat, stirring constantly until slightly thickened but not fully cooked.
Spread a thin layer on banana leaves or a lined tray and steam for 15–18 minutes until set.
Simmer the remaining coconut milk with sugar until dissolved and slightly thick; add a pinch of salt.
Cool slightly, cut into pieces, pour over coconut sauce and sprinkle with toasted sesame.

recipes.name: Vegetarian Seitan Braised with Green Peppercorns
recipes.description: Seitan is pan-seared, then braised with green peppercorns, soy sauce and fresh coconut water. This Bếp Việt vegetarian recipe uses Vietnamese leeks in place of shallots and keeps the sauce lightly reduced for serving with rice.
recipes.serving_basis: Four portions of braised seitan served with hot rice.
recipes.finished_dish: Seitan slices are browned and coated in a lightly reduced, savory-sweet coconut sauce with fragrant green peppercorns.
recipes.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice and spoon the peppercorn sauce over the seitan.
tips: Pat seitan dry so it browns instead of steaming.
Check labels on sauces to ensure they suit your vegetarian diet.
recipes.image_alt: Vegetarian seitan slices braised with green peppercorns in a glossy sauce; transparent background.
search_terms: mì căn kho tiêu xanh chay
ingredients: Cut into 1 cm diagonal slices and pat dry.
May replace with more soy sauce.
Adjust to the sweetness of coconut water.
For searing seitan and frying leek.
preparation_steps: Cut seitan into diagonal slices and pat dry. Rinse peppercorns; separate and lightly crush half.
Mince the white part of the leek. Mix coconut water with soy sauce, vegetarian fish sauce and sugar; taste before braising.
Check sauce labels to make sure they fit the vegetarian diet being followed.
cooking_steps: Heat a little oil and pan-sear seitan until lightly golden on both sides; remove.
Sauté leek until fragrant, add crushed peppercorns and stir briefly. Add the coconut-water mixture and bring to a gentle boil.
Return seitan to the pot, lower the heat and braise for 12–15 minutes, turning gently to coat.
When the sauce is lightly reduced, adjust seasoning, add remaining peppercorns and turn off the heat.
